title: USD and USDZ
sub: Scenes built from layers and variants
cards/0/body:
Pixar open-sourced Universal Scene Description in 2016. It is not just “a file with a model” but a way to assemble huge scenes from hundreds of files.

Each department works in its own layer, and the final scene composes itself.
cards/1/body:
Layers form a stack. If two layers set the same attribute, the stronger one wins: the one higher up.

The chair asset lives in one file, its placement in the scene in another, per-shot tweaks in a third. Nobody touches anyone else’s file.
cards/1/deep: USD strength order is remembered as LIVRPS: Local (opinions in layers), Inherits, VariantSets, References, Payloads, Specializes. A payload is deferred loading of heavy parts of a scene: you open a city and load only the block you need.
cards/2/task: Make the chair red without touching the asset file chair.usda.
cards/3/q: shot.usda says “red”, set.usda says “walnut”. The shot layer is higher. What will the chair be?
cards/3/explain: A stronger layer overrides the opinions of weaker ones.
cards/4/body: A VariantSet is a set of mutually exclusive versions inside one asset: color, level of detail, “regular or bar stool”. Switch it and the scene changes, while the files stay the same.
cards/5/task: You need the walnut chair from set.usda in its bar variant.
cards/6/body:
USDZ is an uncompressed zip archive with USD files and textures inside. Apple uses it for AR Quick Look: open a link on an iPhone and the model appears on your table.

NVIDIA Omniverse is built entirely on USD. Since 2023 USD has been developed by the AOUSD alliance: Pixar, Apple, Adobe, Autodesk, NVIDIA.
cards/7/q: Why is USDZ an uncompressed zip?
cards/7/options/0: The files inside can be read straight from the archive without unpacking
cards/7/explain: The files are also aligned to 64 bytes, so they can be memory-mapped and read right away.
cards/8/q: Where will you run into USD? Select all.
cards/8/explain: USD grew out of film and spread to AR and industrial “digital twins”.
cards/9/pairs/0/1: A file with opinions about attributes
cards/9/pairs/2/1: Bring in another file as part of the scene
